entries.definition: formality and propriety of manner
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names correctness of manner as formality, so the coolness and the holding back are part of what is described rather than praise of it.

entries.definition: formal or perfunctory politeness
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The family's floor: politeness as observed form, either done correctly or gone through with no interest at all, which is why it approves far less warmly than *graciousness*.
examples: his formal civility was just what it had been
hurrying off as if eager to escape from Mrs. Bennet's civilities

entries.definition: a courteous manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The unmarked term for the manner itself, with no standard, object or degree attached; every word beside it adds one of those.

entries.definition: courteous regard for people's feelings
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same courteous regard for feelings as *respect*, but with a yielding in it — the regard shows itself by giving way.
examples: in deference to your wishes

entries.definition: courtesy towards women
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Defined by whom the courtesy is shown to — women — so it marks its object where *courtesy* marks only the manner.

entries.definition: excellence of manners or social conduct
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Not merely meeting the standard of manners but excelling at it, which puts it at the top of this family where *civility* sits at the bottom.

entries.definition: a courteous manner that respects accepted social usage
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plainest name for conduct that respects accepted usage, so mild that the approval barely registers as praise beside *politeness*.

entries.definition: courteous regard for people's feelings
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Aims the courtesy at what another person feels rather than at a code of conduct, so it credits attention where *politeness* credits only correctness.
examples: out of respect for his privacy

entries.definition: overly eager speed (and possible carelessness)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Graver and more formal than *hurry* - the over-eagerness sounds like a fault being named, with the carelessness pressing right behind it.
examples: he soon regretted his haste
He regretted his haste in accepting the first offer he was given.

entries.definition: overly eager speed (and possible carelessness)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word for speed that has got ahead of itself, and it leaves the carelessness a risk rather than a verdict.
examples: He was sorry afterwards for the hurry with which he had written the letter.

entries.definition: a rate (usually rapid) at which something happens
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The bare measure of how fast something happens, with none of the reproach that *haste* attaches to the same quickness.
examples: the project advanced with gratifying speed

entries.definition: a rate (usually rapid) at which something happens
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Names that same rate as a quality something possesses, so it carries a lift of admiration where *speed* stays a flat reading.

entries.definition: any admirable quality or attribute
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same admirable attribute framed as something to a thing's credit, weighable point by point against *fault*.
examples: work of great merit
Miss Bennet eagerly disclaimed all extraordinary merit, and threw back the praise on her sister's warm affection.
construction is not the highest merit, the choicest gift, of the novelist

entries.definition: the high value or worth of something
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Puts the height into the word itself - not worth but worth pitched high, where *worth* names the quality without ranking it.
examples: her price is far above rubies

entries.definition: the quality (positive or negative) that renders something desirable or valuable
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Unsigned by design: it takes the quality positive or negative alike, so it appraises where *virtue* and *fault* have already decided.
examples: the Shakespearean Shylock is of dubious value in the modern world

entries.definition: any admirable quality or attribute
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Presents an attribute as admirable in itself, already judged and approved, where *value* only weighs.

entries.definition: the quality that renders something desirable or valuable or useful
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plainly positive and broad, covering what makes a thing desirable, valuable or merely useful, with none of *price*'s insistence that the quality is great.

entries.definition: the quality of being morally wrong in principle or practice
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The absolute term of the family - it names moral wrongness itself, and covers the principle held as much as the practice done.
examples: attempts to explain the origin of evil in the world
She could not believe there was so much evil in one man.

entries.definition: the quality of being something that holds you back
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults a thing for weighing on you and hampering you, a practical drag rather than the moral verdict *evil* passes.

entries.definition: the quality of an embarrassing situation
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Locates the trouble in the embarrassment of a situation, so the discomfort is felt rather than the ranked shortfall of *inferiority*.
examples: he sensed the awkwardness of his proposal

entries.definition: a failing or deficiency
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the failing inside the thing as something missing or broken, a harder reading of the same deficiency than *shortcoming* gives.
examples: that interpretation is an unfortunate defect of our lack of information
And your defect is a propensity to hate everybody.
it is better to know as little as possible of the defects of the person with whom you are to pass your life

entries.definition: the quality of having an inferior or less favorable position
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain, unheated name for standing lower or less favourably, stating the position without accusing the thing that holds it.

entries.definition: the quality of being a hindrance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Weighs the thing as a hindrance, something in the way of getting on, rather than an emptiness in it as *defect* has.

entries.definition: the quality of being a competitive disadvantage
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sets the thing below its rivals as a matter of competition, judging where *disadvantage* only reports an unfavourable position.

entries.definition: the quality of being limited or restricted
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Marks a boundary — limited or restricted — with no failing charged to anyone, which keeps it flatter than *defect*.

entries.definition: the disadvantage or painful consequences of an action or condition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heaviest here, since the disadvantage comes as painful consequence earned by an action or condition, not merely suffered.
examples: neglected his health and paid the penalty

entries.definition: a failing or deficiency
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Takes the same failing as falling short of a mark, which leaves the thing whole in a way *defect* does not.

entries.definition: a poor example
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Rueful where *excuse* is blunt - the same verdict of inadequacy, delivered with a wince rather than a sneer.
examples: it was an apology for a meal
The cold soup and dry bread were an apology for a dinner.
